note: Media Alias Display overrides entity.media.canonical / entity.media.revision so a file-source media entity's canonical URL streams the underlying file (CacheableBinaryFileResponse) instead of rendering the media page. Requires core media.settings standalone_url=true. Config object media_alias_display.settings has two keys: kill_switch (bool; true = disabled entirely) and media_bundles (sequence of allowed media type ids; empty = all). Settings form at /admin/config/media/media_alias_display (permission administer site configuration). Query args on the alias: ?edit-media (redirect to edit for editors), ?dl / ?download (force download). Medium cases set a known kill_switch / media_bundles value and read it back. Hard cases require enabling the kill switch / restricting to the 'document' bundle, verified against the live config; reset restores shipped defaults (kill_switch=false, media_bundles={}) so verify fails on empty state. No Drush, no own permissions.

evals.prompt: For the Media Alias Display module to work, which core Media setting must be enabled, and where is it?
evals.expected_output: Core Media's 'Standalone media URL' setting must be on (media.settings standalone_url: true, at /admin/config/media/media-settings). Without it a media entity has no canonical URL for the module to override; the status report warns otherwise.

evals.prompt: What are the two configuration options provided by the Media Alias Display settings form, and what does each do?
evals.expected_output: kill_switch (disable the module entirely) and media_bundles (an allow-list of media type ids the file-streaming applies to; empty = all bundles). Stored in media_alias_display.settings; form at /admin/config/media/media_alias_display.

evals.prompt: When viewing a file at its media alias with Media Alias Display, how do you force the file to download, and how do you jump to the media edit form?
evals.expected_output: Append ?dl or ?download to force a download (Content-Disposition: attachment); append ?edit-media to redirect to the media edit form (for users with edit/administer media permission).

evals.prompt: On this site, is the Media Alias Display module actively serving files at their media aliases, or has it been disabled site-wide? Inspect its live configuration to answer.
evals.expected_output: It is disabled site-wide: media_alias_display.settings kill_switch = true (`drush cget media_alias_display.settings kill_switch`).

evals.prompt: Media Alias Display can be limited to certain media bundles. Inspect this site's configuration and state which media bundle(s) it is currently restricted to.
evals.expected_output: It is restricted to the 'document' media bundle: media_alias_display.settings media_bundles contains only 'document'. (An empty media_bundles would mean all bundles.)

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, use the Media Alias Display module's kill switch to disable its file-serving behavior site-wide, without uninstalling the module. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: media_alias_display.settings kill_switch = true. e.g. \Drupal::configFactory()->getEditable('media_alias_display.settings')->set('kill_switch', TRUE)->save(); or tick 'Kill Switch' on /admin/config/media/media_alias_display.

evals.prompt: Configure the Media Alias Display module so that its file-serving behavior applies only to the 'document' media type (bundle), leaving all other media types rendering normally. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: media_alias_display.settings media_bundles restricts to document, e.g. {"document":"document"}. Set with ->set('media_bundles', ['document' => 'document'])->save() or check only 'Document' in the Media Bundles list on the settings form.
